title: Docs: What’s new in BC 28 for developers
summary: Business Central 28 introduces major developer features including semantic search on data and metadata, support for fully qualified names and namespaces in AL, data analysis definitions in apps, MCP Server enhancements, AL coding agents with BC-Bench, improved database index management, and new tooling like the Word Add-in for report layouts and GitHub Codespaces support.
key_points: Developers get semantic search over data and metadata, and analysis views can now be packaged and shipped in AL extensions
New overloads run codeunits, pages and reports and open RecordRefs by fully qualified name; Record and RecordRef also expose FullyQualifiedName
MCP tooling grows, including an Admin Center API MCP server usable from VS Code and a standalone MCP server in ALTool
New tooling covers index usage management, a Word Add-in (preview) for report layouts, GitHub Codespaces and a faster Base64 codeunit; the new SFTP Client module is being withdrawn by Microsoft
Many new compiler, CodeCop and AppSourceCop rules cover analysis views, native procedures, BigInteger conversions and FlowFields in query links
features: semantic search on data and metadata

quotes.text: AL developers can use semantic search on data and metadata. Allow developers to define data analysis definitions in their apps.
quotes.why_it_matters: Highlights core developer capabilities for intelligent data access and custom analysis tools in BC 28

quotes.text: New method overloads are introduced to support running codeunits, pages, and reports using their fully-qualified names.
quotes.why_it_matters: Demonstrates namespace support enabling more explicit and maintainable code organization patterns

quotes.text: BC 28 provides tools to view index usage statistics and selectively disable low-use indexes to improve write performance and reduce storage costs.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows new performance optimization capabilities for production environments
